The main takeaway from our work is that

the vocalisations of the eastern quoll can be objectively classified into a set of five vocal types that can be used to better understand the species' social interactions and to improve the detection and identification of vocalisations recorded in the wild.

objective methods can be used to objectively classify and quantify vocalisations, and that this approach may be particularly useful for species with vocalisations that are difficult to distinguish by human listeners.
vocalisation types can be objectively defined for dasyurids and that this approach will facilitate the use of automated bioacoustic monitoring techniques for this group of animals.
